Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **The message history closes on phones**: it has a close button, closes when its newest line is pulled up past the end, and scrolls smoothly by dragging and flicking
- **Back is the game's Esc** on Android and in a phone's browser: it closes the history, a panel, a prompt or a screen, and on the title asks whether to quit
- **Movies have their sound on Android**: a movie plays its sound from a file beside it there (the opening's `opening.opus`), since Android's movie player can lose it
- **The save and load screens scroll** through all 90 slots instead of turning nine pages
- **Save and load in one click** from the quick menu's SAVE and LOAD (right-click or long press), Continue shows the save's picture, and the wheel over the volume panel changes the music's volume
- **Every screen can be left with taps alone**, checked on every platform; a message window's own buttons can fade when the pointer is away (`buttonsfade=`)
- **The quick menu's pin works on Android**: unpinned by a tap, the strip goes at once and its handle brings it back
- The strip below the game on Android is black, not white
- An effect or animation shown on a layer after a movie played there is no longer cut off at the movie's size, and rewinding in the browser goes all the way back to the scene's start
- kagex-release 0.21.0 downloads the 0.21.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.21.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
